transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
High winds and heavy rain from a nor'easter continue to batter the coast, flooding streets and knocking out power.
National Weather Service meteorologist Frank Pereira says the storm is stalled offshore.
"The storm itself is centered off the New Jersey coast, the Long Island coast, and it's going to continue to sit there for the next day or so, just kind of drifting in the area.
And as it does, it will continue to bring coastal impacts and unsettle weather across portions of the mid-Atlantic to New England through the remainder of the weekend."
In Hawaii, Hurricane Nolo is moving away from the islands, though its effects have disrupted travel.
Danielle Mendoza was trying to fly out of the Big Island.
"We're trying to go to Oahu and southwest shutdown, so we have to buy ticket to Hawaiian Airlines, looks like."
Farther east in the Pacific, Hurricane Nolo is bearing down on Mexico's Baja California peninsula.
Forecasters expected to make landfall on Monday as a weaker storm.
California Governor Gavin Newsom signed a package of gun safety bills Saturday.
Lakshmi Sarah of member station KQED reports.
The ten new laws include one that funds intervention programs to interrupt violence,
and another requiring that 3D printers sold in California block attempts to make ghost guns.
There's also one that creates a statewide office of violence prevention.
Mike McLively is the policy director of the Gifford Center for Violence Intervention.
"There's a lot of state-level infrastructure now to support cities and community-based organizations doing that violence intervention work,
but we didn't have a designated office, and this will now create a director of community violence intervention."
The California Rifle and Pistol Association opposed the bill on 3D printing guns,
calling it "a costly, impractical, and constitutionally problematic burden."
For NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Sarah.
Pope Leo told a massive crowd gathered at the Shrine of the Lourdes that the Catholic Church must confront deep wounds caused by clergy abuse.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports the pontiff is continuing his trip to France.
Lourdes is a town in the foothills of the Pyrenees Mountains that attracts some three million pilgrims a year
for its purported healing spring waters on the spot where a 19th century shepherd girl had apparitions of Virgin Mary.
The site is also connected to a recent scandal.
The Shrine's facade has a series of mosaics by a prominent religious artist accused of abusing 20 women.
The stories tall mosaics have been covered for the Pope's visit.
Leo has previously apologized for abuse scandals that have damaged the church's credibility.
On a trip to Spain in June, he told bishops they must listen to survivors and offer reparations.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
This is NPR.
With the midterm election just over a month away, some Democrats are focusing on faith as an issue that might sway voters to their side.
NPR's Jason DeRose reports a noteworthy number of Democratic candidates are clergy.
In Texas, Baptist pastor Frederick Haynes is running for an open U.S. House seat in the Dallas area.
And Presbyterian seminary student James Talarico is the Democratic nominee for Senate there.
A Methodist pastor is the Democratic Senate nominee in Kansas.
And a Lutheran pastor and a Presbyterian chaplain are running as Democrats for two different U.S. House seats in Iowa.
Pew Research has found that fewer than one-third of Democrats say religion is important to them,
but communities vary widely, and these candidates appear to be gaining traction.
The Cook Political Report has moved the Texas Senate seat and one Iowa House district from Lien's Republican to Tossup.
Jason DeRose, NPR News.
A whistleblower says renovations at the Kennedy Center were rushed, and some of the work was poorly done.
The allegations include rusting steel columns and a bathroom floor replaced because President Trump disliked its color.
The center is now closed for a larger renovation amid a separate fight over Trump's effort to add his name to the building.
A federal judge has blocked that change, saying it requires congressional approval.
The judge, in the case, has also ordered the center to give 30 days notice before making major structural changes.
I'm Windsor Johnston, and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
That's plus.npr.org.
